Package org.checkerframework.framework.stub

Class BinaryStubsCommandLineTest

java.lang.Object
org.checkerframework.framework.stub.BinaryStubsCommandLineTest
public class BinaryStubsCommandLineTest extends Object
End-to-end tests for the reader side of binary -Astubs support: AnnotationFileElementTypes's parseCommandLineStubLocation, parseCommandLineStubResource, commandLineBinaryStub, and the useBinaryForCommandLineStubs gate. org.checkerframework.framework.stubifier.BinaryStubFileGeneratorTest covers only the writer (round-tripping per-file and bundle output); this class drives real compilations through TypecheckExecutor, the same harness CheckerFrameworkPerDirectoryTest uses, so it exercises the reader with dynamically generated fixtures that a checked-in jtreg test cannot have (a checked-in .astub.bin.gz would defeat the point of a content digest).

Uses the SubtypingChecker with the test-only Encrypted qualifier ( org.checkerframework.framework.testchecker.util.Encrypted) rather than a real checker like Nullness, so this test stays entirely within the framework module (Nullness lives in checker, which depends on framework, not the other way around). A stub-annotated Lib.maybeEncrypted() returns either @Encrypted Object (if its stub's annotation took effect) or the default, unqualified Object (if it did not); passing the latter where @Encrypted is required is an argument.type.incompatible error, so that error's presence or absence is a direct, unambiguous signal of whether the stub was applied at all -- from either its text or its binary form.

    • bundleNameCollisionWithPerFileSiblingIsIgnored

      public void bundleNameCollisionWithPerFileSiblingIsIgnored() throws IOException
      A directory stubs passed to -Astubs can coincidentally share its bundle's target name (stubs.astub.bin.gz, beside it) with an unrelated top-level file stubs.astub's own per-file sibling (also named stubs.astub.bin.gz, since stubs.astub's sibling-naming rule appends the same suffix to a name that already ends in .astub). binaryStubBundleFor must recognize, via the magic number, that the file at that path is not actually a bundle, and silently fall back -- without misapplying anything and without a spurious diagnostic -- to per-file siblings, which still work normally for files genuinely inside stubs/.
      Throws:
      IOException

    • freshPerFileBinaryPassesDiffCheck

      public void freshPerFileBinaryPassesDiffCheck() throws IOException
      A fresh per-file binary also passes the framework's own differential check ( -AbinaryStubDiffCheck, from BinaryStubDiffChecker in framework-test), which independently text-parses the same .astub file and compares every annotation it applies against what the binary form applied. This is a second, more exhaustive layer of verification than this test's own has(java.util.List<javax.tools.Diagnostic<? extends javax.tools.JavaFileObject>>, java.lang.String) assertions: it catches a binary whose annotation resolution is silently wrong, not merely absent.
      Throws:
      IOException

    • mergeStubsWithSourceTextParsesTheAnnotatedJdk

      public void mergeStubsWithSourceTextParsesTheAnnotatedJdk() throws IOException
      Under -AmergeStubsWithSource, text parsing of the annotated JDK applies the annotations of the private classes that the minimized JDK keeps (such as java.util.AbstractList.Itr), which the binary stub file omits. The annotated JDK is then text-parsed, so the differential check, which compares the two whenever the binary is read, finds no mismatch.

      IOException

    • incompleteJarSetupWarns

      public void incompleteJarSetupWarns() throws IOException
      A .jar with a binary sibling entry for only some of its .astub entries still applies the covered entry's binary form, text-parses the uncovered one, and warns about the incomplete setup -- the JAR-entry analogue of incompleteBundleSetupWarns(). Also confirms that a JarEntryAnnotationFileResource, not just a FileAnnotationFileResource, participates in that accounting.
      Throws:
      IOException

    • jarBinarySiblingDirectoryEntryIsIgnored

      public void jarBinarySiblingDirectoryEntryIsIgnored() throws IOException
      A .jar entry whose only "sibling" at the expected binary name is a directory entry (e.g. Lib.astub.bin.gz/, not a real file) is treated as having no binary form at all, not misread: JarFile.getJarEntry(java.lang.String) silently falls back to matching name + "/" when the exact name is absent, so parseCommandLineStubJarResource must reject a directory match explicitly. Also confirms this falls back to text parsing rather than throwing, since a real archive with a stray directory entry at that path (e.g. from a mis-packaged build) must still compile successfully.
      Throws:
      IOException
